articles.title: Ferrari Reveals Lewis Hamilton Brake Fix Attempt as Charles Leclerc Hints at Mystery Issue
articles.summary: Frederic Vasseur says Ferrari tried to solve the brake pedal issue of Lewis Hamilton in F1 Spanish GP, as Charles Leclerc reveals a late tyre mystery. It did...
articles.body:
Frederic Vasseur says Ferrari tried to solve the brake pedal issue of Lewis Hamilton in F1 Spanish GP, as Charles Leclerc reveals a late tyre mystery.

It didn't take long for Ferrari's Hamilton to face issues with his brakes in F1 Spanish GP at Madring. As Red Bull debated with Max Verstappen about giving the place back to the Brit after cutting the corner on Lap 1 to take track position, the seven-time champion had his own issues to deal with.

That's why it delayed Verstappen all the more when he slowed to give the place to Andrea Kimi Antonelli and Hamilton . But he could immediately re-pass the Brit due to his brake issues. Team principal Vasseur said they tried to fix the issue remotely from the pit wall.

It was back to normal when Hamilton continued on for another lap. But it came back, and they didn't wish to risk it anymore. "Honestly, I don't know, because they were working on the car when I left [for the media call]," said Vasseur to media after F1 Spanish GP. "Yes, the pedal was long, but we tried to fix it from the pit wall, it came back, and once again.

"I think in this kind of track, we also don't want to take any risk, and it was, we are on Lap 1, it was still 56 to go. Yes, it was Lap 1 or Lap 2, I think. The first time that happened was Lap 2, and it was too risky to go to the next lap. It would have made no sense, to take a crazy risk," summed up Vasseur.

With Hamilton's side done, focus shifted to Leclerc. The early Virtual Safety Car meant the Monegasque went long in his hard tyre stint. There was the long hope of a safety car or red flag stoppage to help him, but nothing arrived and he had to pit eventually. Vasseur reckons the pace was there in the car.

Ferrari Insists Issue Is Qualifying Position Rather Than Race

It is qualifying that Ferrari needs to work on, as known. "The race was more than good, we did a stint of 49 laps, 49 I think, with the hard and the pace was still there," said Vasseur. "But honestly, we took a bet, but all the teams did the same, with one car in soft or medium, another one in hard to cover all the options.

"He was leading the group of hard, and I think with the second incident, the red flag, it was the win. With a safety car, he would have been P2, P3, nothing like P4, but it's more a strategy than something else. On his side, the pace was good, it's the only thing that we can do on Sunday. Honestly, if we miss something, it's more qualifying, or perhaps a little bit in Monza, or yesterday.

"But today, I think we did what we have to do, but we took the risk that we have to take, and the pace is the pace that we need to have," summed up Vasseur, as Leclerc noted a mysterious issue on the soft compound that halted his push late in the Grand Prix.

He was all good on the hard compound but wasn't able to catch the back of Lando Norris despite having the fresh tyre and softest compound. "Yeah, I mean obviously Bryan [race engineer] and I didn't speak too much during the race because on a track like this I just wanted to have as little communication as possible, but at one point I just checked to understand exactly what we were fighting for because I didn't really know inside the car," said Leclerc.

"But yeah, at the end of the day I think the pace was quite strong on the hard, on the soft at the end I couldn't really push for other reasons, but the hard stint was a good one, eventually where we are paying the price, it's our qualifying pace, because when you are starting further away then you get to the race and it's very difficult to make up those positions."

When asked to share what the issue was, Leclerc smiled but did not wish to share. "No, not really, no I can't, but it's fine, I mean it will be fine for the next race," he said, adding that the strategy was correct from Ferrari, as they couldn't have done anything else other than this.

Leclerc also clarified that Hamilton did not hold him up at the start when he had the brake issues. "No, I mean he did it very, very quickly obviously," he said. "I wasn't losing so much time because obviously with the brake problems he was kind of cutting the corners, so he didn't hold me up and wouldn't have changed anything in my race."

Now that Gabriel Jesus has opened his account with FC Barcelona following a transfer from Arsenal , his next task is to continue getting minutes.

For the moment, his fellow Brazilian, Raphinha , has been the team's starting striker. Raphinha, a winger usually, has excelled in the role after Barcelona let Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres leave in the summer.

Barça pursued Julián Alvarez throughout the transfer window, but Atlético Madrid did not budge in efforts to sign the player.

Jesus has been affected by injuries over the last few years. Most observers peg him as a backup option for Barcelona, at least at first.

Recently, the forward was asked whether he saw himself as a starter or Raphinha in his place.

"Rapha is doing really well as a number nine; he has great ability to play there—he's proving it and scoring goals, which is the main thing. I also know that the season is very long and that I'll have opportunities to play," he said.

For the moment, there's no suggestion Raphinha would stop starting as a striker. He's in red-hot form, banging in goals. But with Barcelona playing multiple games across different competitions, Jesus will likely have chances to start in addition to substitute appearances.

articles.title: ‘We Always Get Better’ – Jonathan Haggerty Credits Brother Freddie’s Discipline In Crushing Win At The Inner Circle 30
articles.summary: "The General" was in his brother's corner in Lumpinee Stadium, and he was beaming with pride.
articles.body:
ONE Bantamweight Kickboxing World Champion Jonathan "The General" Haggerty had a ringside view of his brother Freddie Haggerty 's toughest assignment yet, and he could not have been happier with how it played out.

The younger Haggerty overcame Rungruanglek TN Muaythai via unanimous decision in their strawweight Muay Thai battle at The Inner Circle 30 in Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium this past Friday, September 11.

Freddie dropped Rungruanglek twice across the opening two rounds, first with a counter left hook off the ropes, then with a follow-up left hook to the temple off an exit from the clinch.

Rungruanglek tried to weather the storm with digging elbows and working Freddie's legs, but the 21-year-old Englishman stayed composed on the back foot, picking the Thai knockout artist apart with sharp counters until the final bell.

The unanimous decision snapped Rungruanglek's five-fight winning streak and pushed Freddie's record to 25-5 overall, marking his second straight victory of 2026 on the subscriber-exclusive Asia primetime card.

Though Freddie fell short of his pre-fight prediction of a knockout, Jonathan had nothing but praise for the performance he watched unfold.

"It was a great performance. It was pushing for the stoppage, but we didn't get it. It is what it is. It's all love; it's a learning curve. In this sport, you can never stop learning, so we'll go back to the drawing board. [We will] work on things that didn't work and get better each time."

The missing knockout mattered far less to Jonathan than the person who did show up at The Inner Circle 30. Freddie stuck to the game plan from bell to bell, and that discipline stood out more than any finish.

Patience is not always the easiest thing to preach in a sport built on highlight-reel finishes, but "The General" sees real value in his brother choosing execution over urgency.

"I wasn't disappointed that he didn't get the knockout because if you go for the knockout too much, you rush, and things might not go your way. "I'm happy with his discipline, the way he stepped back, picked him off. We'll get the stuff [sorted] for sure. We always get better. Every performance we do, we do better."

"I wasn't disappointed that he didn't get the knockout because if you go for the knockout too much, you rush, and things might not go your way.

"I'm happy with his discipline, the way he stepped back, picked him off. We'll get the stuff [sorted] for sure. We always get better. Every performance we do, we do better."

Jonathan Haggerty Gears Up For His Own World Title Defense

With Freddie's night behind him, Jonathan Haggerty shifts his attention toward his massive assignment on the global stage of martial arts next month.

The reigning ONE Bantamweight Kickboxing World Champion puts his crown on the line against former divisional king Hiroki Akimoto in the main event of ONE SAMURAI 4 inside Tokyo's Ariake Arena on Saturday, October 17.

Jonathan has never been one to shy away from bold declarations ahead of a fight, and this time is no different.

The 29-year-old English firecracker offered:

"I'm more than ready. Fans can expect fireworks, explosiveness, and a knockout."

Beyond the bravado, Jonathan has not lost sight of who has helped carry him to this point in his career.

A run this long – spanning multiple weight classes and two disciplines – does not happen in isolation, and he has always been quick to credit the people standing behind him every step of the way.

The bantamweight kickboxing king concluded:

"Thank you so much for always supporting me for years now. You guys are a big part of ONE Championship. Fans pick you up when you're down. They make you positive. That extra bit [of motivation] just spurs you on."

articles.title: Cowboys at Giants Stock Report: Christian Parker, Javonte Williams lead disappointments
articles.summary: Here is our stock report following Sunday’s loss
articles.body:
The wounds had just healed. We all had moved on from the 2025 Dallas Cowboys and their historically bad defense. The team seemed to do this as well, especially with regards to action. The Cowboys front office operated this entire offseason, as it seemed, with a pledge for things to never be as bad as they just were.

Sunday night was a total and complete disaster did not go well for the Cowboys. In their first opportunity to prove that things were different, they gave life to the notion that maybe the present is simply more of the past.

To make matters worse, unlike last season the offense is now under a bit of fire. They were not as bad as their defensive counterparts at MetLife Stadium (hardly saying anything), but ultimately the collective team has apparently taken an entire step back.

We are starting with positives, there are a few, and need to give credit to someone who had as much negative press as anybody when training camp began: Tyler Guyton.

NFL Pro's insights noted after the game that Guyton recorded 20 pass-blocking matchups against Brian Burns in this game. He did not allow a single pressure. Overall Guyton allowed just a pair of pressures on 36 total pass blocks in the game. He lived up to the challenge. That is great news.

It is obviously difficult to feel positive about much on defense, but Caleb Downs was as advertised.

The sack he made was the clear flash, but he held his own and was hardly why the defense got worked the way that it did. The sky is very high for him as we all believed.

It was around a week ago when we all found out that Tyler Smith would miss at least a month due to his thumb injury. Given that Smith is the best interior lineman in the NFL, there was a natural level of concern.

Give T.J. Bass credit, though. Many expected him to be serviceable in Smith's absence, the Cowboys did place a second-round tender on him after all, and he was. That is hardly an easy thing to do.

You would have a very difficult time finding someone who had a longer honeymoon after initially joining the Cowboys.

From January to Sunday afternoon, Christian Parker was heralded. He came from a strong lineage, said all of the right things, and he was given plenty of new tools to reconstruct the defense that was so bad last season. Sunday night was just one game and he could still wind up fulfilling the proverbial prophecy, but wow his group was overwhelmed.

Grading the game in a vacuum it was about as big of a failure as it possibly could have been. Time to move on.

There are only so many ways to say this, and we have all said it:

What are you doing taunting? In general! Down by a touchdown still?

Responses I've seen to this vary, but the most defensive of Williams seem to be that the NFL is soft and that taunting penalties are lame. Fine if you feel that way. But Williams knows the rules.

Arguably more importantly, Brian Schottenheimer knows the rules. They all have to operate within them and didn't, and it literally costed the team a point.

Williams was not the only player to commit a silly penalty. Recall that DeMarvion Overshown hit Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart clearly out of bounds early in the game. These are silly and avoidable mistakes.

Those things start with the head coach, and Brian Schottenheimer has also been riding a bit of a positive wave for the last few months. I'll speak for myself and say that I am willing to give him a bit of a mulligan for last season with how the front office went about handing things to him, but I put zero blame on the front office here in 2026. They have done their job. This is on the people who coach and play the games.

Schotty has to get things in check as soon as possible.

It feels unfair to penalize Brandon Aubrey for missing an extra point after Javonte Williams pushed him back, but he is now paid very handsomely. Expectations rise when things like that happen.

What's more is this continues to pick at the notion that maybe Aubrey has lost his fastball a little bit. He's not always down the middle anymore on his kicks, even when making them. Concern feels somewhat warranted.

Let us first say that we hope DeMarvion Overshown recovers quickly from his hamstring injury. Before he left the game though, Overshown was not exactly shining for on-field performance reasons. He had the penalty and was then critically missing just about every read. He was a high point of weakness in the heart of the defense.

We are almost two years removed from when Overshown really shined for the Cowboys. Right now it is looking like this may not be in the cards. We will see.

Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart threw for 3+ touchdowns without any interceptions for the first time in his career on Sunday night. This is only his second NFL season and it's not like he even started every game last year, but obviously that is pretty damning of the Cowboys defense.

Consider that the highest point of pressure came from Caleb Downs as noted. The Cowboys were not able to generate any frustration for Dart up front and that inability led to them getting pushed around all game long.

Where were Donovan Ezeriuaku and Rashan Gary ? How were they not more frustrating to deal with?

Objectively speaking, the Cowboys have beaten up on the NFC East for much of the Dak Prescott era. Specifically, they have pushed around the Giants whenever they wanted.

This was just one game to be clear, but it was not the meaningless contest that Dallas lost to New York in Week 18 last year. The Cowboys gave this game all of their might and the new-look Giants humbled them mightily.

Next week will bring another test of this variety. The Washington Commanders took the Philadelphia Eagles the distance a few hours before the Cowboys failed against the Giants, and one of Washington and Dallas will fall to 0-2 by this time next week.

articles.summary: For the first time since 2009, both the New York Giants and New York Jets have started the season 1-0.
articles.body:
The New York Giants and New York Jets accomplished a feat in Week 1 that had not been done since 2009.

Both teams won their season openers for the first time in 17 years. The Giants opened with a 28-20 victory over the Dallas Cowboys , while the Jets earned a 23-10 win over the Tennessee Titans .

For the Giants, quarterback Jaxson Dart threw three touchdown passes. Isaiah Likely had an eventful debut, leading all Giants receivers with 78 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Francis Mauigoa did not allow a sack or pressure, and Deonte Banks made a statement with commendable coverage against Cowboys star CeeDee Lamb , recording two passes defensed.

The Jets received a strong performance from quarterback Geno Smith in his return to New York .

The last time both teams won their openers was in 2009, when the Giants defeated Washington 23-17, and the Jets beat Houston 24-7.

The rare start gives both teams early momentum, and New York fans renewed optimism heading into Week 2.

articles.title: Hawaii's all-time wins leader makes coaching change after 0-4 start
articles.summary: Hawaii's winningest high school football program fired coach Tupu Alualu after an 0-4 start to the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Hawaii's all-time winningest high school football program has made a coaching change following a winless start to its 2026 campaign.

A report from the Honolulu Star-Advertiser's Paul Honda Monday afternoon stated that Saint Louis (HI) has dismissed Tupu Alualu in the middle of his third season with the program.

The report states that Saint Louis school president Glenn Medeiros sent a letter out to families informing them of the decision and that Leonard Lau will serve as the team's interim head coach starting immediately.

"We are grateful for the time and dedication Tupu has given to our young athletes, and we thank him for his contributions," Medeiros wrote in the letter. "After careful consideration, we have made the decision to move our football program in a new direction. We wish Tupu all the best in his future endeavors."

In 2024, Alualu led the Crusaders to Hawaii's Open Division state championship despite starting the year 1-2. Last season, Saint Louis finished 5-3.

This season, in a schedule featuring Super 25 programs such as No. 2 IMG Academy and No. 16 Sierra Canyon , the Crusaders are 0-4 and have been outscored 155-12 in four games. They've suffered three straight shutouts, scoring their only points in a 20-12 season-opening loss to Kahuku.

With the coaching change, Leonard now takes over the high school program where he once played as a wide receiver. Following his playing days at Saint Louis, Leonard went on to play at the University of Hawaii.

Since his playing days ended, Leonard has served as an assistant coach at Aiea, Kamehameha and Punahou. During his time at Punahou, he served as the interim head coach for a year before another hire was made.

"We are grateful to Coach Leonard for accepting this interim role," Medeiros continued in the letter to the families. "We are confident he will serve as a strong, positive role model to our young Saint Louis School gentlemen."

The Crusaders have 22 overall state championships dating back to 1983. From 1986 to 1998, they won 13 straight championships, and in the current format, they've won eight state titles since 1999, including a four-peat from 2016-2019.

articles.title: Arch Manning had a good laugh over AI edit of Steve Sarkisian slapping Holly Rowe
articles.summary: Steve Sarkisian blowing off ESPN reporter Holly Rowe after Texas’s comeback win over Ohio State on Saturday was bad form, and he received plenty of pushback...
articles.body:
Steve Sarkisian blowing off ESPN reporter Holly Rowe after Texas 's comeback win over Ohio State on Saturday was bad form, and he received plenty of pushback in the days since.

In the Longhorns locker room, however, it sounds like it's been all laughs and giggles over the incident.

Texas quarterback Arch Manning met with the media on Monday to discuss his performance in the come-from-behind victory after he led the Longhorns on three touchdown drives in the fourth quarter.

At one point, Manning was presumably asked about the incident after the win, in which Sarkisian blew off Rowe during the post-game interview opportunity, gave the camera the Horns Up gesture, and then ran off (this coming after he was curt with Laura Rutledge at halftime ). While many called the move rude and classless , that was apparently nothing compared to what people were doing with the clip online.

"I've seen a few AI edits and stuff, but that's about it. I saw AI edits of Sark's interview," Manning told reporters on Monday. After someone in the room referenced a specific AI version, Manning asked, "Have ya'll seen that one? That's a good one," and laughed, adding, "Of him slapping Holly Rowe?"

As the mention of a video showing the Texas coach slapping a female ESPN reporter makes a few other people in the room chuckle, Manning turns to someone off camera before looking forward and adding, "It's hilarious."

One would think it would go without saying that admitting publicly that you thought a video of your football coach slapping a woman was hilarious is a bad idea, but we live in "interesting times." Even the X post sharing the clip, from On3's Inside Texas reporter Evan Vieth, sells his answer as "gold."

The 22-year-old may not be a full-grown man yet, but he should know better, and it reflects poorly on the adults in that room and on the Texas coaching staff that they'd all feel comfortable joking about something like that, especially given the Manning family's history around football and sexual harassment allegations . To say nothing of the fact that we're weeks out from the Good Good Golf controversy that effectively ruined that company .

It's a bad look for Manning, a bad look for Texas football, and a bad look for men in general at a time when that's unfortunately par for the course.

articles.title: Lions hoping Jahmyr Gibbs can stay as productive despite losing backfield partner
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions know they are asking a lot of star running back Jahmyr Gibbs.  For the first three years of his career, Gibbs was paired with David Montgom...
articles.body:
DETROIT (AP) — The Detroit Lions know they are asking a lot of star running back Jahmyr Gibbs .

His next major test will come Thursday against the Buffalo Bills .

For the first three years of his career, Gibbs was paired with David Montgomery in Detroit's "Sonic and Knuckles" partnership. Montgomery wasn't a little-used backup, either. He averaged 853.3 yards and 11 touchdowns over the past three seasons.

Montgomery picked up where he left off Sunday, scoring three touchdowns, but that was for the Houston Texans in a 36-31 loss to the Bills.

At the same time, Gibbs was dealing with his new workload as Detroit's only experienced rusher. He averaged a career-high 18.8 touches per game last season, but got 34 in Sunday's 31-30 overtime win over the New Orleans Saints — three more than his previous high.

He made the most of them, rushing for 156 yards and two touchdowns while adding 30 yards on five receptions, but now he's facing a short week before facing the Bills in their home opener.

"I told him to drink a lot of Gatorade," Lions coach Dan Campbell said Monday. "If this were a normal week, Thursday would be the day our guys were fully recovered and we'd be going full speed at practice. This week, we'll be at full speed and jumping right into a game."

This early in the season, Campbell isn't too worried about Gibbs.

"I think Gibbs is going to be recovered for Thursday," he said. "I think he'll be ready to go, just like the rest of our guys, and he'll have plenty of juice in the tank."

"I'm good," he said after the game. "I feel fine. I could have taken 40 (touches) today."

Detroit's backup is special teams regular Sione Vaki , who has only carried the ball nine times in 28 career games.

Detroit's new-look offensive line, with rookie Blake Miller at tackle and Juice Scruggs at center, looked good. The Lions carried the ball 33 times for 165 yards and two touchdowns, and Jared Goff was only sacked once.

Detroit's defense dominated the first 38 minutes of the game, forcing Tyler Shough into three turnovers, and helped the Lions build a 21-0 lead.

In the next 31 minutes, though, Shough went 25 of 33 (75.8%) for 325 yards and three touchdowns as the Saints forced overtime and then had a 2-point conversion attempt that would have won the game.

That's a problem, considering the Lions face Josh Allen on Thursday.

Outside linebacker Derrick Barnes intercepted a pass on the first play of the second half, setting up a Lions touchdown, then helped stop New Orleans ' 2-point conversion attempt in overtime by getting into the flat quickly enough to take away Shough's passing lane to Chris Olave .

Wide receiver Jameson Williams dropped multiple passes, including a deep throw from Goff that could have been a 67-yard touchdown. Williams also fumbled a pitch-out on an end-around.

He did redeem himself slightly with a 22-yard catch to the Saints 5 to set up Detroit's overtime touchdown.

While Detroit's offensive line played well, it is not clear if two of the five starters will be available Thursday. Monday's injury report indicated that guard Christian Mahogany (hip) and Miller (knee) would not have practiced.

"It's a short week, so it is really about how fast we can get them back out there," Campbell said. "They've got the normal recovery period and the injuries on top of it. We'll know more tomorrow. but it is a situation where Friday would be better than Thursday."

578 — The number of touches Gibbs will get if he averages the same workload he had on Sunday. His career high is 320, set last season.

The Lions don't have the kind of offensive-line depth to replace two starters, especially on a short week, so the training staff will be working feverishly to get Mahogany and Miller ready for the Bills. Buffalo has won five straight matchups with the Lions, but each game has finished with a one-score margin.

articles.title: India pacer Mukesh Kumar joins Nottinghamshire for two County matches
articles.summary: Mukesh Kumar was the highest wicket-taker in this season's Duleep Trophy, capturing 12 wickets at an impressive average of 14.91.
articles.body:
In-form India pacer Mukesh Kumar has joined Nottinghamshire and will play the final two fixtures of the 2026 English County Championship season. Mukesh has 26 international caps across all formats, including three Test matches, in which he has taken 32 wickets. "I am really pleased to sign for Nottinghamshire at an important time in the season. I can't wait to arrive in England and test myself in county cricket," said Mukesh in a release issued by the club. "I want to contribute as much as I can while I am here to help Nottinghamshire to success, and I am looking forward to working with the coaches and my new teammates," he added.

His stint at Trent Bridge will be the first time in his career that he has represented a domestic side away from Bengal. "Coming to England is always a good challenge, and I am excited by the chance to play for a new team in new conditions," he said. "I will give everything while I am part of Nottinghamshire, and I hope together, we can be successful."

Mukesh comes in after strong Duleep Trophy

Nottinghamshire head coach Peter Moores said: "We're really excited to get Mukesh over at what is a crucial time of the season. He comes straight off the back of a really competitive game in the Duleep Trophy final, in which he was on the winning team and played a pivotal role in securing the win for East Zone." Mukesh was the highest wicket-taker in this season's Duleep Trophy, capturing 12 wickets at an impressive average of 14.91. "Mukesh's quality as a bowler is not in question, knowing how hard it is to compete to play in the Indian team. "It's fantastic for us to get a player who's match-ready and in full competitive mode ahead of two big games for the club," Moores added.
